title: Server Side Rendering (SSR)
definition: SSR is the process of rendering a client-side application (like React) into fully populated HTML on the server on every request. When the client receives it, the browser downloads the JS bundle and 'hydrates' the HTML to make it interactive.
simpleExplanation: Instead of sending the browser an empty box and instructions on how to build the toy, the server builds the toy, paints it, and ships it fully ready to play with.
diagramContent:
sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser
  participant S as Node Server
  B->>S: GET /dashboard
  Note over S: Fetches DB data
  Note over S: Renders React to HTML String
  S-->>B: Fully Populated HTML
  Note over B: User sees UI instantly (FCP)
  B->>S: GET bundle.js
  S-->>B: bundle.js
  Note over B: React Hydration (App becomes interactive)

answers.question: Define Server Side Rendering.
answers.answer: Server Side Rendering is a critical architectural pattern in frontend design.

answers.question: What is the main tradeoff of Server Side Rendering?
answers.answer: Usually a tradeoff between Server CPU usage, TTFB (Time to First Byte), and Client CPU usage.
